stage.name: Portugalete to Castro Urdiales
stage.narrative: You cross a provincial border today but not a cultural one — the Basque-speaking world ends somewhere around Kobaron. By midday you are in Cantabria and the road signs are only in Spanish. Castro Urdiales is your reward: a perfect medieval port with a 13th-century Gothic church (Santa María de la Asunción) sitting on a rock above the harbour, looking exactly like a fortress-church should. The sun on the church at the end of a 32 km day is one of the Norte's great moments.
stage.closing: Three regions now — Gipuzkoa, Bizkaia, Cantabria — and you have not yet walked a thousandth of the Camino. What is the long walk teaching that a short one could not?
